data.exact_reserve_text: Of the adverse claims movement of GBP 3.4m in the year ended 31 December 2015, GBP 0.4m related to the older years 2006-2010 which appear to have achieved a degree of stability, GBP 2.2m to the 2011 year of account and GBP 0.8m to the pure year of account.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse claims movement related to older years (2006-2010) amounting to GBP 0.4m, though described as appearing to have achieved a degree of stability.
Adverse claims movement on the 2011 year of account of GBP 2.2m, identified by the signing actuaries and incorporated into reserves.
Adverse movement of GBP 0.8m attributable to the 2012 pure year within the 2012 year of account.

Uncertainty over significant potential Australian tax rebates (2012: between GBP 3-GBP 3.5m under review; 2013: AUD1m reopened return) influenced the decision to put years into run-off and not to recognise the rebate as an asset.

named_events.loss_description: One of two main CAT events in CY15 giving rise to a gross loss of GBP 4.8m and net loss of GBP 1.8m (largest was Storm Desmond).

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2015 the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding (31 Dec 2014) was GBP 32.218m. During 2015 reserves were strengthened, primarily due to adverse development in the liability (casualty) portfolio driven by volatility and an external actuarial reassessment; extracting the gross claims development triangle indicates a net prior year strengthening of approximately GBP 6.30m (19.5% of opening reserves). The managing agent also cited reserve methodology/IBNR recalibration and uncertainty over potential Australian tax rebates as material factors. Separately, property catastrophe activity in 2015 (notably Storm Desmond) produced material gross/net losses noted in the report.
raw_causal_phrases: continued uncertainty over the final loss arising from a combination of factors, the most material being a potential tax rebate of GBP 2.8m, not held on the balance sheet, and a continuing assessment of the reserving position due to volatility experienced.

Of the adverse claims movement of GBP 3.4m in the year ended 31 December 2015, GBP 0.4m related to the older years 2006-2010 which appear to have achieved a degree of stability, GBP 2.2m to the 2011 year of account and GBP 0.8m to the pure year of account.
78% of the movement in the claims in CY15 arises from a move to further strengthen the liability class of business given adverse movement experienced in older years of account.
The reason for placing the 2012 year of account in to run-off was due to a significant level of Australian tax rebates being sought for this year of account.
The two main CAT events have given rise to a gross loss of GBP 4.8m and net loss of GBP 1.8m.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (6.295m) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle printed in the Technical Provisions note (gross triangle values converted from GBP '000 to GBP m). The report does not provide a single labelled 'movement in prior year's provision' gross figure; narrative and per-year breakdowns for the 2012 YOA provide complementary information. Aggregate '2010 & prior' column was excluded per instructions. Some table alignment in the PDF extract required interpretation; amounts rounded to three decimals where converted.
